lines.text: Japan designed a pyramid... about fourteen times taller than Giza.

shots.prompt: A colossal glass and steel lattice pyramid rising out of Tokyo Bay, so tall its peak pierces the clouds, tiny ships on the water at its base, dawn light.
shots.motion: Camera rises fast up the face of the colossal lattice pyramid from the water toward its cloud-wrapped peak. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

lines.text: Two thousand metres high. Rising out of Tokyo Bay.

shots.prompt: The Tokyo skyline seen across the bay, dwarfed by a gigantic open-frame pyramid on the water, its upper half above the clouds, golden hour.
Looking straight up one edge of a vast pyramid made of a geometric steel lattice, the edges converging far into the sky.

lines.text: A single structure... for one million people.

shots.prompt: Inside a gigantic pyramid made of open lattice, a vast airy space filled with suspended towers, gardens and light, small crowds far below.
shots.motion: Slow drifting camera through the vast interior of the lattice pyramid, light beams shifting, tiny transit pods gliding along the struts. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

lines.text: Thirty-storey skyscrapers... hanging inside the frame.

shots.prompt: Several 30-storey skyscrapers suspended by cables inside a giant pyramid lattice, hanging in mid-air with lit windows, people on sky bridges.
Close-up of thick dark cables holding a skyscraper in the air inside a geometric frame, clouds visible through the lattice.

lines.text: Moving walkways. Inclined elevators. Robot pods running through the struts.

shots.prompt: Futuristic accelerating walkways and inclined glass elevators inside a colossal lattice structure, people travelling, warm light.
Small automated transit pods racing along the inside of giant steel struts in a pyramid city, motion blur, bright interior.
shots.motion: Transit pods race along the struts, light streaks behind them, camera follows smoothly. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

lines.text: Building it would take eighty years... and materials still being invented.

shots.prompt: Robotic construction arms assembling a gigantic lattice of dark carbon struts over the sea, a half-finished pyramid frame, overcast sky.
Macro view of a glowing black carbon nanotube cable, futuristic laboratory light, shallow depth of field.
Present-day Tokyo Bay at dusk, calm water, distant city lights, empty horizon where nothing rises, soft fog.

lines.text: But imagine, for a moment... that it was.

shots.prompt: Present-day Tokyo at night seen from the bay, a colossal glowing lattice pyramid two kilometres tall rising from the water, its upper half above the clouds, millions of lights inside.
shots.motion: Slow upward crane shot rising along the glowing pyramid, clouds drifting around its middle, lights twinkling inside. The architecture stays rigid and unchanged.

lines.text: It would be more than twice as tall as anything on Earth.

shots.prompt: A colossal pyramid beside a modern supertall skyscraper for scale, the pyramid more than twice as tall, dramatic sky.
View from the peak of a two-kilometre pyramid above the clouds at sunrise, Mount Fuji in the distance.

# Short #003 - The Shimizu Mega-City Pyramid

## Title options (1 = recommended)
1. Japan Designed a Pyramid 14 Times Taller Than Giza
2. A City for a Million People Inside One Pyramid
3. The 2-Kilometre Pyramid Japan Never Built

## Description
Two kilometres high. A million residents. Skyscrapers hanging inside the frame.

Japan's Shimizu Corporation designed the Mega-City Pyramid for Tokyo Bay: a 2,004-metre structure with suspended 30-storey towers and transit pods running through its struts. It needs materials that are still being researched, and it was never built. This is a concept visualization of what might have been.

Visuals are AI-generated concept art, not photographs or plans of a real structure.
